summary: A structured, part-time, fully remote 3-month training internship for UK students, starting 16 December 2026, with 30 places and monthly 1-to-1 check-ins. Build a project every week in Linux, Proxmox, Ansible, Docker, Kubernetes and MLOps.

sections.title: About Sheerwater Studios
sections.text: Sheerwater is a UK infrastructure and AI consultancy based in Woking, Surrey. We design and build on-prem, cloud and local AI infrastructure for research groups, startups and small organisations, using Linux, Proxmox, VMware, Ansible, Kubernetes and Terraform.

sections.title: About the programme
sections.text: This is a structured, part-time, fully remote 3-month training internship, not a job in the usual sense. Each week has one live evening session of about 2.5 hours, then a project you build in your own time and push to GitHub. There are 30 places, with monthly 1-to-1 check-ins and written feedback on every project. It is voluntary and unpaid, it does not involve client work, and it does not lead to an accredited qualification. You finish with a GitHub portfolio, a statement of completion and a clear record of what you built.

sections.title: Dates
sections.text: The first session is on Wednesday 16 December 2026. There are no sessions on 23 and 30 December, then weekly sessions resume on Wednesday 6 January 2027. The final showcase is on Wednesday 17 March 2027.

groups.label: Weeks 1 to 7: foundations
items: Git, GitHub and the Linux command line (weeks 1 to 3)
Linux administration: users, permissions, SSH, systemd, networking, storage and Bash scripting
Proxmox: virtual machines, templates, networking and backups, with a VMware comparison (weeks 4 to 5)
Ansible: inventory, playbooks, roles, patching and hardening (weeks 6 to 7)

groups.label: Weeks 8 to 12: modern platforms
items: Docker: images, containers, volumes and Compose (week 8)
Kubernetes: pods, deployments, services, ingress, configuration and monitoring (weeks 9 to 10)
MLOps: serve and monitor a small local AI model (week 11)
Capstone showcase evening and feedback (week 12)

sections.title: What you'll do
items: Build and harden a Linux server, and write a backup and health-check script
Build a Proxmox lab, back up and restore a virtual machine, and write a short migration plan
Automate setup and patching across several servers with Ansible
Containerise an app and deploy it to a Kubernetes cluster
Run a small local AI model behind an API with simple monitoring
Document every project so someone else can follow it

sections.title: What you'll get
items: A live session every week, monthly 1-to-1 check-ins and written feedback on every project
A GitHub portfolio of about 10 small projects and one capstone
Project descriptions for your CV and LinkedIn
A statement of completion from Sheerwater Studios, and a reference from the founder on successful completion, where earned

sections.title: Who this suits
items: Studying or recently graduated in computing, IT or engineering, or teaching yourself
Curious about servers, Linux and automation. No prior experience required.
Able to commit around 8 hours a week for 3 months, with breaks for exams
A laptop with 16 GB RAM, or willingness to use a shared lab host
If you are under 18, we ask for a parent or guardian's consent

applySteps: Share your LinkedIn profile. It takes about a minute.
We read every application and reply by email.

title: AI Business Analyst (Associate)
summary: A voluntary, part-time advisory role for a business analyst who wants hands-on experience with private AI projects, working as and when you are available.
metaTitle: AI Business Analyst (Associate): voluntary part-time role, remote UK

facts: Part time, on and off. No set hours.

sections.title: About Sheerwater Studios
sections.text: Sheerwater is a founder-led UK infrastructure and AI consultancy based in Woking, Surrey. We sell fixed-scope services including on-premises infrastructure, Azure and AWS landing zones, Kubernetes, and private AI that runs on a client's own systems. We are early stage and building our first client work.

sections.title: About the role
sections.text: The AI Business Analyst helps us decide which problems are worth solving with private AI, and shapes how we scope, test and report on each pilot. It is a voluntary advisory role for someone with business analysis experience who wants to work on AI projects alongside a small team. You choose what to take on and when.

sections.title: What you could work on
items: Discovery: build a standard discovery questionnaire and requirements template for our services, starting with the private AI pilot
Use-case selection: help a client find one task where AI will save time, and define what a good result looks like
Pilot testing: plan and run testing sessions with a client's team and write a short verdict report
Data and risk review: map where a client's data sits and what must stay in-house
Proposals: turn discovery notes into a one-page proposal and statement of work
Training programme: help keep our student programme organised
Hands-on AI: build a prompt library and test our local AI demo, using Claude and other tools

sections.title: Who this suits
items: Experience in business analysis: stakeholder interviews, requirements, process mapping and documentation
Interest in AI, and ideally some project experience with chatbots or similar tools
Clear writing, and confidence talking to non-technical people
Reliable communication: you tell us when you are busy, and we do not chase
No deep technical background needed

sections.title: What you get
items: Real AI project experience for your CV and LinkedIn, with a title and a short written reference where earned
Practice with Claude and other AI tools on real business tasks
A say in how our private AI offer is shaped

sections.title: How it works
items: Part time, on and off. There are no set hours, no minimum commitment and no deadlines we can enforce.
Either side can stop at any time, without notice or reason.
This is unpaid and is not employment. It creates no contract of employment, and we make no promise of future paid work.
Client information stays confidential, and we ask you to confirm this in writing.

applySteps: Share your LinkedIn profile. GitHub is optional. No CV needed.
We read every application ourselves and reply by email.

title: Project Manager
summary: Keep our remote engineering interns organised, on schedule and talking clearly with the UK.
about: You are the day-to-day link between the founder in the UK and our team of engineering interns. You turn written scopes into plans, keep everyone unblocked and make sure clients get honest, regular updates. You do not write production code.
work: Break each project scope into weekly plans, tasks and milestones
Run a short daily stand-up and a weekly demo with the UK
Track progress, risks and blockers, and raise them early
Write clear weekly status reports that the founder can share with clients
Match interns to tasks and help new starters settle in
Keep the project board, meeting notes and handover documents up to date
requirements: Based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Applications from outside Dhaka cannot be considered.
A degree in any subject; a business, IT or engineering degree is a plus
At least two years coordinating software, IT or similar project delivery
Good fluency in written and spoken English, as most communication is in English
Confident using a task board such as Jira, Trello or Linear
A working understanding of agile ways of working (sprints, stand-ups, retrospectives)
Reliable, organised and calm when plans change
Able to give feedback kindly and clearly, and to say when something is at risk
nice: A project management qualification such as PRINCE2, PMP or a Scrum certificate
Experience supervising students or junior staff
Basic understanding of cloud, DevOps or web development
trial: A paid task: turn a short sample scope into a two-week plan with risks and a status report.

title: DevOps and Platform Engineer Intern
summary: Learn to build cloud, Kubernetes and automation for real client infrastructure projects.
about: Work alongside an experienced technical lead and the founder to build the infrastructure that other software runs on. You will start with small, well-defined tasks and take on more as you grow. Everything you build is reviewed before it reaches a client.
work: Write Terraform and Ansible to set up cloud and Linux servers
Help build and harden Kubernetes clusters
Create CI/CD pipelines that test and deploy software automatically
Set up monitoring with tools such as Prometheus and Grafana
Document every build in a runbook that clients can follow themselves
Take part in weekly demos and explain what you built
requirements: Based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Applications from outside Dhaka cannot be considered.
Minimum: a completed bachelor's degree (or final-year student finishing within six months) in computer science, IT, engineering or a related field
Good fluency in written and spoken English
Working knowledge of Linux on the command line
Basic scripting in Bash or Python
Understanding of Git and version control
Basic knowledge of networking: IP addresses, DNS, firewalls, SSH
Careful habits with passwords, keys and changes to live systems
Willing to explore new, fun challenges and to learn by building, breaking and fixing things
Curious, patient and honest about what you do not yet know
nice: A home lab, virtual machines or personal projects you can show us
Experience with Docker, Terraform, Ansible, Azure or AWS
Progress towards a certification such as Azure Fundamentals, CKA or Terraform Associate
trial: A paid task: deploy a small app to Kubernetes from a Git repository, with an automatic pipeline.

title: AI and Machine Learning Engineer Intern
summary: Help deploy private, self-hosted AI systems that run on a client's own servers.
about: We help organisations use AI on their own data without sending it to third parties. As an intern you will help set up, test and measure open-weight language models and document search tools, with guidance from senior colleagues.
work: Run and test open-weight language models on local and GPU servers
Build document search tools that answer questions using a client's own files
Prepare and clean data for search and evaluation
Measure answer quality and write up what works and what does not
Package models and tools in containers so they are easy to deploy
Help prototype AI agents where a human approves every action
requirements: Based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Applications from outside Dhaka cannot be considered.
Minimum: a completed bachelor's degree (or final-year student finishing within six months) in computer science, data science, AI, mathematics, engineering or a related field
Good fluency in written and spoken English
Solid Python, including working with libraries such as NumPy or pandas
Understanding of the basics of machine learning and how large language models work
Comfortable using Linux and the command line
Understanding of Git and version control
A habit of testing claims and checking results before reporting them
Willing to explore new, fun challenges, including problems nobody has solved before
Respect for data privacy and confidentiality
nice: Experience with tools such as Ollama, vLLM, LangChain or vector databases
A thesis, project or portfolio involving machine learning
trial: A paid task: run a local model with a simple question-and-answer interface over a handful of PDF files.

Plan and schedule a regular calendar of posts, and write clear, friendly captions
Turn technical project updates and screen recordings into simple, engaging stories
Add subtitles, graphics and our brand look to every piece
Track what performs well and suggest what to make next
Help produce launch announcements and recruitment posts

Skill with a video editor such as Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut or CapCut
Good eye for pacing, sound, text and simple motion graphics
Comfortable with Canva or Figma for thumbnails and post graphics
Willing to explore new, fun challenges and try new formats and trends
Reliable with deadlines and happy to take feedback

Basic understanding of social media analytics and scheduling tools
Interest in technology, cloud or AI, and the ability to explain it simply
Basic photography, audio or motion-graphics skills (After Effects or similar)
